sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Financials stand out as the sole sector with clean, multi-horizon positive breadth, while Technology and Energy maintain the highest absolute momentum despite narrow market participation.

The US sector landscape shows highly concentrated strength, with only the Financial sector (momentum 0.65) achieving "all-green" status across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD). Meanwhile, Technology (momentum 0.817) and Energy (momentum 0.700) continue to lead absolute momentum rankings, with Tech clawing back one spot to rank 2 over the last five sessions.

Conversely, defensive and cyclical laggards continue to drag, led by Utilities at a weak 0.167 momentum score. We are also seeing early signs of fatigue in Basic Materials, which dropped 1 spot to rank 3 over the past week despite holding a relatively strong momentum score of 0.67.

## Strength
* **Financials Stand Alone:** Financial is the only sector (1 of 11) to achieve all-green breadth across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and YTD, carrying a momentum score of 0.65 (rank 7).
* **Tech and Energy Lead Absolute Momentum:** Technology (0.817 momentum, rank 2) and Energy (0.700 momentum, rank 1) remain the strongest absolute momentum drivers in the market.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Technology & Communication Services Advancing:** Technology rose 1 spot to rank 2 (momentum 0.82) and Communication Services gained 1 spot to rank 9 (momentum 0.45) over the past 5 sessions.
* **Utilities & Materials Slipping:** Utilities fell 1 spot to rank 10 with a weak momentum of 0.17, while Basic Materials also dropped 1 spot to rank 3 (momentum 0.67).
* **Persistent Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom (rank 11) with a momentum score of 0.350, closely trailed by Consumer Defensive at rank 8 (momentum 0.333).

## Divergences
* **Basic Materials Fading:** Basic Materials represents a key early-warning divergence, slipping 1 spot to rank 3 over the last 5 sessions despite its high overall momentum score of 0.67.
* **Narrow Breadth:** With only a single sector (Financials) displaying all-green breadth, market participation remains narrow despite strong top-line momentum in Technology and Energy.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Narrow market breadth persists as only 17 of 143 groups maintain all-green status, led by dominant energy and industrial sectors, while consumer retail and renewable utilities experience sharp weekly declines.

Narrow leadership remains the defining feature of the market, with traditional energy and industrial groups holding firm at the top. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.94) and Coking Coal (momentum 0.88) continue to lead the 17 all-green industries. Meanwhile, software and thermal energy are seeing a notable weekly rotation, with Software - Infrastructure and Thermal Coal both surging 16 spots in rank.

In contrast, consumer cyclicals and green energy are fading rapidly. Specialty Retail plummeted 28 spots to rank 104, and Utilities - Renewable dropped 23 spots to rank 108. This weakness aligns with broader momentum laggards like Footwear & Accessories (momentum 0.05) and Solar (momentum 0.13), indicating a clear risk-off stance regarding retail and clean energy.

## Strength
* **Constrained Breadth:** Only 17 of 143 industry groups are all-green across all timeframes (weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD).
* **Top Performers:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.94) and Coking Coal (momentum 0.88) lead the sustained strong list, showing robust multi-month momentum.
* **Secular Leaders:** Staffing & Employment Services (momentum 0.87) and Marine Shipping (momentum 0.85) remain highly resilient as top-tier all-green industries.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Software - Infrastructure jumped 16 spots to rank 64 (momentum 0.78), matching a 16-spot rise in Thermal Coal (rank 72, momentum 0.76). Coking Coal and Consumer Electronics both improved by 15 spots.
* **Sharpest Decliners:** Specialty Retail fell 28 spots to rank 104 (momentum 0.20), while Utilities - Renewable dropped 23 spots to rank 108 (momentum 0.19).
* **Momentum Bottom:** Footwear & Accessories (0.05) and Airports & Air Services (0.07) continue to anchor the bottom of the momentum rankings.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups are starting to slip in rank, led by Shell Companies (-10 spots, momentum 0.61), Diagnostics & Research (-5 spots, momentum 0.74), and Oil & Gas E&P (-5 spots, momentum 0.66).
* **Emerging Defensives:** Low-momentum groups are quietly climbing the ranks, led by Utilities - Diversified (+8 spots, momentum 0.35) and Household & Personal Products (+6 spots, momentum 0.45).
